quote: A game that starts slow is often a game that's starting on the wrong foot.
title: Just Let Them Play!

quote: With games in particular, players really want to take control and find out about your game— so it's no time for ambling along. Let them play, first thing!
title: Start with the Climax

quote: This might sound like an exaggeration, but I'll say it anyway: To make players wait is a sin!
title: Say No to Slow!

quote: The time players spend in a game is a cost, so it's best to be mindful of the time they're choosing to give you.
title: Be Mindful of the Time Players are Giving You

quote: Come storm or dark of night, the one thing you should never change is your trajectory toward that light.
title: Staying True to Your Concept

quote: What you really want to avoid is having to change course because your game's not fun.
title: Spec Changes

quote: There should always be an ideal spec to start, and from there you can course-correct to maximize cost effectiveness.
title: Don't Rely on a "Plan B"

quote: As long as you move through a dense presentation quickly, page count itself isn't really an issue.
title: Writing Game Proposals

quote: Tutorials shouldn't feel like work, or like they're slowing down the beginning of the game— instead, try to weave them into the game's progression itself.
title: Making Tutorials Feel Natural

quote: In your proposal and your final product, do your best to let things shine in a way all their own.
title: Avoiding Comparison
